notes: REF-BM-02: pageReader.js's readPage() only ever derives a title from the URL slug and a favicon URL; description is always '' and thumbnail always null (readPage always returns limited:true) — two of the four auto-collected fields are stubbed, never populated. REF-BM-04: openModal renders the URL as a static <div class="murl"> (app.js:360), not an input — url is not editable in the editor. REF-BM-14: search box (matchesQuery in store.js) does plain whitespace-split substring matching against raw label text; there is no '#' prefix parsing to target tag search specifically (tag filtering is only done via clicking sidebar labels, a separate UI, not via typed '#tag' syntax). REF-BM-15: no boolean/parenthesis grammar exists anywhere in matchesQuery/applyFilter — AND/OR/NOT is only exposed as UI toggles (include/exclude sets + all/any mode), not as operators parsed from the search string, and there's no rule to treat quoted operator words as literal. REF-BM-16: no quote-parsing logic in matchesQuery — query is naively split on whitespace, so a quoted phrase is not treated as an exact contiguous match. REF-BM-23: note-writing exists (textarea, stored, shown on card and in the copy reader) but is always rendered via esc()-escaped plain text (app.js labelRow/openCopyReaderPanel) — no markdown parser is present, so markdown syntax is never rendered. REF-BM-24: capture.js explicitly does not create an HTML snapshot file; it returns a canned readable-text body for exactly 3 hardcoded demo domains (smittenkitchen.com, use-the-index-luke.com, github.com) and 'none' for everything else, with no PDF-vs-HTML branching at all. REF-BM-25: archiveUrlFor() only builds a passive web.archive.org search-results link; it never triggers creation/submission of a new archive snapshot. REF-BM-31: no export/serialization code exists anywhere in the codebase (only import parsing, confirmed via grep for 'export'/'netscape' producing no writer function). REF-BM-32: there is no settings/preferences UI or persisted user-settings entity — the sort dropdown is a transient view-state control, not a saved default, and there is no displayed-items-count or font-size control.
